thread.title: Nasdaq Tries End Losing Streak; Why Retail Stocks Show Strength

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Nasdaq Tries End Losing Streak; Why Retail Stocks Show Strength
text:
U.S. stock indexes started Friday on a weak note and a rebound was cut short amid news that the U.S. plans to increase tariffs on China. Retail stocks led.
X Stocks fell sharply after noon ET on reports that President Trump is preparing tariffs on another $267 billion worth of Chinese imports, on top of $200 billion already planned.
In the meantime, Canada and U.S. trade talks struck an uncertain note. Trump could proceed with a Mexico-U.S. trade agreement and leave out Canada, but that remained unclear.
The Nasdaq was down 0.1% after being down three sessions in a row, including two days of sizable losses in the tech-heavy index. Intraday, the composite index rallied as much as 0.5%.
Blue chips slouched as the Dow Jones industrial average was off nearly 0.5%. The large cap S&P 500 fell 0.2%. Small caps edged up 0.1% in the S&P 600.
Volume declined on the Nasdaq and the NYSE. The Nasdaq was poised to end a three-day losing streak.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Among IBD's 197 industry groups , retail, software security and chip designers were among the day's top gainers. The retail sector has delivered the most new highs in the previous three sessions.
The Retail Stocks Reaching New Highs Retail stocks hitting new highs Friday morning included O'Reilly Automotive ( ORLY ), Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ), restaurant operators Wingstop ( WING ) and Texas Roadhouse ( TXRH ), Costco Wholesale ( COST ), BJ's Wholesale Club ( BJ ), Ollie's Bargain Outlet ( OLLI ) and variety store chain Five Below ( FIVE ).
Retail stocks either in or above the 20% to 25% profit-taking zone include Costco, O'Reilly and Wingstop. Research shows that stocks often begin to consolidate after a post-breakout gain of 20% to 25%, so taking profits there is prudent.
In IBD's Big Cap 20 screen , winners led losers by a 3-to-2 ratio. Big Cap 20 member Apple ( AAPL ) was on track to end two days of losses. Apple rose about 1% in fast trade.
The exchange traded fund Innovator IBD 50 ( FFTY ) advanced 2%. The fund, which is based on the IBD 50, jumped 37% last year but is up only 14% this year.
Financial Data The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported 201,000 jobs added in August. This topped the Street's consensus estimate by 3%. Meanwhile, the jobless rate remained unchanged at 3.9%.
Average hourly earnings year over year grew 2.9%.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose seven basis points to 2.94%. The 2-year yield was at 2.7%, and the 30-year yield was 3.1%.
The CME FedWatch Tool puts the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate hike this month at 99.8%. For December, the likelihood for an additional hike after September is pegged at 77.6%.
